messages:
andrea b: FYI opened a docs PR to fix inconsistent tier boundaries in examples and the SDK snippet. dashboard shows friendly ranges but examples used inclusive upper bounds so 10,000 ended up in the wrong tier. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4933

mike r: can we adopt a single rule in docs? i'd prefer half-open intervals [min, max) to match metering pipeline semantics.

cheng li: +1. i'll update `docs/reference/quotas.md` and add a tiny table showing the mapping.

sam_k: also noticed the SDK v7 example in `/snippets/quotas/sdk_v7.md` used header `X-RW-Quota: 1000` without units. i'll add comment and both curl + node examples.

lia: UX note: keep pretty labels on the Grafana panel (e.g., "1k - 10k") but add a tooltip: "rounded label; actual interval is half-open [min, max)." i can push a panel-annotation quick PR.

andrea b: sounds good. action items: cheng update docs text + examples, sam update SDK snippets, lia add tooltip, mike verify public billing CSV link in the migration guide.

mike r: checked the migration guide link, swapped the internal sheet for public export: https://docs.redwood.ai/public/billing-tiers.csv. i'll also add sha256 to the docs so integrators can verify downloads.

cheng li: pushed small change: added sentence "All tiers use half-open intervals: [min, max). Values equal to max belong to the next tier." and updated the sample mapping table.

sam_k: updated snippet. short curl + node bits: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage/calc -H "X-RW-Quota: 1000 (requests)" -d '{"user":"acct-999","requests":10000}'
``` ```js
// Node example
await client.post('/v1/usage/calc', { headers: { 'X-RW-Quota': '1000 (requests)' }, body: { user: 'acct-999', requests: 10000 } });
```

lia: panel-annotation PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4936 1: tooltip text matches wording.

andrea b: great. will wait for CI & l10n. merging checklist: docs text, SDK snippet, panel tooltip, CSV link + checksum, l10n approval. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
